summary: A Long Way Up! is an interactive web-based game in which you and up to 3 other players form a team, and carry out space missions from concept all the way to implementing it. It gives students such as ourselves and many other audiences an open-source way to explore how missions are carried out and planned through just like in real life. A web-based game meaning it does not need specific hardware requirements. The game is designed to be accessible and a fun and educational experience for kids and grown ups alike.
details: A Long Way Up! is a simple webpage-based interactive experience about bringing space missions from concept to application. Having a web-based app increases its accessibility for all users. We want it to have lasting educational impact those who'll play it, have an educational space journey through laying out how space missions are brought to practice. Github repositories are mainly used as the codespace in HTML for the main webpage, JavaScript for the game experience, and CSS for styles. The fabrication of game was made with Github Copilot. SI was not used in brainstorming and idealization, rather, only in coding, debugging, and making the game feel more smooth. This project explores carrying out space missions as a fun collaborative experience whilst considering real life engineering decisions and not taking these lightly as they can influence the success of the mission. We acknowledge that this isnt a one man job to do space missions, we made a rough model of how collaborative gameplay should be, for now, only local players can experience this in multiplayer. We assigned roles that are also crucial in the real life application. Employee, picking out missions for the team. Engineer, plan out and pick the necessary trade-offs for the success of the mission. Mechanic, construct the launch vehicle by picking out the most viable components. Astronaut, execute the necessary training to keep you in shape for training. Scientist, analyze how well (or how bad) your mission went. All in all, this game is the fruit of our ambition, efforts, and passion for this.
